marks.gloss_en: [the half-gourd] -- does it become a handle for its fellow?
a fig-tree branch that broke and remains attached by its bark -- R' Yehuda deems pure
[the branch] -- does it become a handle for its fellow?
a corner stone: when he extracts, he extracts all of it; when he demolishes, he demolishes his own and leaves his fellow's
[the stone's part] -- does it become a handle for its fellow?
as death does not make a replacement, so all [of the animal] that does not make a replacement imparts impurity
דתניא: יכול יהא בשר הפורש מן החי טמא? תלמוד לומר וכי ימות מן הבהמה -- מה מיתה שאינה עושה חליפין ...
if so [that 'min habehema' includes part of an animal], then flesh [separating from the living] too?
לא סלקא דעתך, דתניא -- it should not enter your mind, as it is taught: flesh separating from the living is excluded (= p_basar_min_hachai_tahor)
it should not enter your mind [that flesh from the living imparts impurity]
as an animal is sinews and bones, so all [separated from it] that is sinews and bones imparts impurity
as an animal is flesh, sinews and bones, so all [separated from it] that is flesh, sinews and bones imparts impurity
R' Akiva: 'animal' -- as an animal is sinews and bones, so all that is sinews and bones
'when they are dead': as death does not make a replacement, so all [of the sheretz] that does not make a replacement imparts impurity
might flesh separating from sheratzim be impure? the verse says 'when they are dead' -- as death does not make a replacement, so all that does not make a replacement
as a sheretz is sinews and bones, so all that is sinews and bones imparts impurity
as a sheretz is flesh, sinews and bones, so all that is flesh, sinews and bones imparts impurity
R' Akiva: 'sheretz' -- as a sheretz is sinews and bones, so all that is sinews and bones
but this verse is needed for the other teaching of Rav (some of an animal imparts impurity and some does not: a slaughtered tereifa)
'and if [any] of the animal dies' -- some of the animal imparts impurity and some does not; which is that? a tereifa that one slaughtered

R' Asi to R' Zeira: what was said in the study hall?
what [difference] is there between a limb from the living and a limb from a carcass?
flesh that separates from a limb from the living does not impart impurity
a limb from the living, which imparts impurity -- what is the verse?
what [difference] is there between Rabbi and R' Akiva?
between R' Akiva and R' Yosei HaGelili, what is [the difference] between them?
between Rabbi and R' Akiva the knee joint is [the difference]

had it taught us [only] the animal -- the reason it does not impart [impurity] from life would be that it does not impart in a lentil-bulk; but a sheretz, which imparts in a lentil-bulk, say it imparts from life

and had it taught us [only] the sheretz -- because it does not impart by carrying it does not impart from life; but an animal, which imparts by carrying, say it imparts from life. [Both are] necessary
one who severs an olive-bulk of flesh from a limb from the living -- severed it and afterwards designated it [as food] -- it is pure
designated it, and afterwards severed it -- it is impure
